rounds.text: Connplex Cinemas Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, as evidenced by a severe disconnect between its aggressive expansion and short-term institutional outflows [E4, E8]. The company accelerated its operational footprint in FY26 to 41 cinemas and 113 screens across 9 states, driven by an impressive addition of 30 screens in H2FY26 alone [E20, E21]. Furthermore, management has secured a robust pipeline of 230+ upcoming screens planned across FY27 and FY28 [E22], demonstrating a clear pathway to scaling its presence. This aggressive network expansion is already translating into explosive operating metrics, with total footfalls surging by approximately 63% year-over-year to 27.63 lakh admits [E26], alongside rising Average Ticket Prices of INR 264 [E27] and improved Spend per Head of INR 95 [E28]. Backed by an almost nil total debt position [E29] and a comfortable net cash reserve of INR 7,615 lakhs as of March 2026 [E30], the company possesses pristine financial flexibility to fund its long-term vision of operating around 1,000 screens by 2030 [E37] without balance sheet strain. Conceded: E23, which shows that EBITDA margin contracted by 377 bps to 23.68% in FY26 due to front-loaded operational and expansion-related costs.

The bear case for Connplex Cinemas Ltd centers on significant institutional capital flight and a contraction in core profitability metrics despite rapid expansion. Foreign institutional holdings dropped from 2.47% to 0.72% and domestic institutional holdings fell from 8.08% to 6.96% between September 2025 and March 2026, driving a negative money flow signal of -2.87 percentage points [E2, E3, E4]. This sustained institutional outflow directly triggered a neutral rules-based screen score of just 49 out of 100 [E7, E8]. Concurrently, the company's EBITDA margin for FY26 contracted by 377 basis points YoY down to 23.68% due to escalating operational and expansion-related overheads [E23]. This margin compression occurs against a backdrop where sector median ROCE languishes at a low 5.6% and sector median profit growth sits in negative territory at -3.5% [E11, E13]. Furthermore, internal scaling has nearly doubled employee headcount from 96 to 143, pushing employee costs up sharply from INR 5.24 crore to INR 9.95 crore [E24, E25]. Conceded: the company operates with an almost nil total debt position and a comfortable net cash reserve of INR 7,615 lakhs as of March 2026, alongside robust footfall growth of 63% [E26, E29, E30].
